name: EPA/ECHO regulatory escalation state
mechanism: A facility moving through an environmental regulatory state machine (inspection/evaluation -> violation/noncompliance -> significant noncompliance -> enforcement action -> settlement/remediation) may reveal a regulator's escalating assessment of operational/legal exposure before an issuer summarizes that exposure in periodic corporate disclosure. The object is the stage transition and cross-program escalation state, not a generic ESG score or raw violation count.
event_clock: Earliest reproducible public ECHO state/record boundary from an immutable historical snapshot. Current ECHO refreshes weekly, so no same-day or publication-time claim is allowed until a historical snapshot clock is proven; otherwise use the next regular trading-session boundary.
cheap_falsifiers: raw event counts add no structure beyond size/industry/regulatory-exposure controls
state labels are fully explained by firm size, industry, prior violations or already-public issuer disclosure
issuer mapping is not historically stable under frozen FRS relationships
weekly ECHO refreshes cannot yield a defensible public-observation boundary
corrections or re-reporting rewrite the historical prefix
the apparent information state disappears after conservative SEC/news observability controls
useful fields require paid EPA data
gates: historical ECHO and ICIS-FE&C archive census
exact historical public-refresh/publication boundary or conservative next-session rule
violation/enforcement correction and revision lineage audit
source_basis: EPA FRS Download Summary and Data Element Dictionary: https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads/frs-download-summary
Le, EPA Enforcement Actions and Property Prices, Accounting & Finance (2026), DOI 10.1111/acfi.70222
From facilities to balance sheets: Environmental reputational risk and financial leverage, Finance Research Letters (2026), DOI 10.1016/j.frl.2026.110601
notes: Discovery/source-feasibility lead only. This file does not establish PIT validity, ranking, performance authorization or promotion.

EPA ECHO provides inspection/compliance, violation, enforcement and penalty information; downloads are typically refreshed weekly, while all years of EPA formal enforcement-action data are available through the Enforcement Case Search.
FRS provides a unique facility identifier and cross-program linkage, with organization and parent relationships. Name/ownership changes make historical identity stability an explicit gate.
The mechanism is deliberately framed around regulator-state transitions and escalation, not a generic environmental score or raw event count.
